description: The Landscape Performance Series Case Study Briefs are a searchable database of over 200 built landscape projects with quantified environmental, economic and social benefits. The Landscape Architecture Foundation produces them with designers and academic research teams who assess each project's performance, alongside a fast fact library and a benefits toolkit. Briefs can be filtered by benefit (stormwater management, flood protection, urban heat, carbon, habitat, property values, maintenance savings and more), by feature (bioretention, green roof, green wall, permeable paving, rainwater harvesting, wetland, trees) and by tags such as resilience, with grid and map views. Coverage is mainly North America with projects elsewhere. Format and access: web pages and downloadable briefs. Licence: not stated on the page read; free. Caveats: projects are chosen as exemplary, and benefits are measured with differing methods, so they are not a random sample. It gives evidence for climate adaptation design of green-blue infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the susdrain SuDS case studies and the CIRIA SuDS Manual.
